records.name: Friends of Jefferson Square Park
records.summary: Neighbors who look after Jefferson Square Park on Washington Avenue in Pennsport. They hold a park cleanup on the second Saturday of the month and welcome ideas for the park.
records.what_you_do: Join the monthly cleanup to tend the planting beds and pick up litter, come to the park's film nights and holiday lighting, or send in an idea for the park.

schedule.text: Cleanups on the second Saturday of the month, March through December, weather permitting. The events list shows 9 to 11 am, and the about page says 9 am to noon.

cost.text: No fee is listed for cleanups or events. The group asks for donations to care for the park.

first_step.how: Come to the second Saturday cleanup at 300 Washington Ave, March through December. No sign-up is listed for cleanups.
first_step.basis: Cleanups are announced to the public and anyone can come. The site has no first-time welcome or newcomer program, so it does not reach 4.
first_step.what_to_expect: A cleanup lasts about two to three hours on a Saturday morning, weather permitting. You pick up litter and tend the planting beds alongside neighbors who look after the park. No fee is listed to join, though the group asks for donations.
first_visit_tips: Cleanups run March through December and stop in winter, so check the events page for the next date before you go.
Join the email list or the Facebook group to hear about changes to a date.
If you have a question first, use the contact form on fojsp.org.

records.notes: Website fojsp.org is confirmed as this group's own site (address, cleanup dates, events, contact form). The about page gives cleanup time as 9 am to noon and the events list gives 9 to 11 am, so schedule.text shows both. The email pprstewardship@phila.gov is the City stewardship address from the City list. The group's contact page has a form and lists no email, so the City address is kept and flagged for review. Dated items (Oct 10 and Nov 14 cleanups, Oct 13 ribbon cutting, Dec 5 holiday lighting) are left out of schedule and what_you_do; the newest dated item is the Oct 10, 2026 cleanup listing, which sets last_sign_of_life. The Facebook and Instagram links come from the contact page.

records.name: Friends of Jewish Cemeteries
records.summary: A volunteer effort of the Jewish Federation of Greater Philadelphia that restores Jewish cemeteries, including Har Nebo in Oxford Circle. Volunteers clear brush and trash, help with headstone work alongside professionals, and help digitize burial records.
records.what_you_do: Help with cleanups, which include cutting back vines and weeds and picking up trash, or join the headstone and plot work or the records project. Some volunteers help digitize about 26,000 records and cards at Har Jehuda.

schedule.text: The page lists no set volunteer days or hours. It says cleanups are currently taking place at Har Nebo and Har Jehuda.

locations.label: Har Nebo cemetery, Oxford Circle, Northeast Philadelphia

cost.text: The page lists no fee to volunteer. Donations go to the cemetery restoration fund.

first_step.how: Email Jeffrey Lasday at jlasday@jewishphilly.org and ask to be added to the volunteer mailing list for work days.
first_step.basis: The group is open to community members and neighbors and gives a named contact and a mailing list to join. The page does not describe a beginner program or set work days.
first_step.what_to_expect: Work days are not published, so the first step is a conversation with the group's contact. Typical tasks are cutting vines, pulling weeds and picking up trash, and stone lifting and repair are done with a certified professional. The page lists no fee to volunteer.
first_visit_tips: Ask before you come how long a work day lasts, what to bring or wear, and whether children may join, because the page does not say.
Headstone repair is heavy work done with professionals, so ask which tasks a newcomer would do.
Har Nebo is in the Oxford Circle neighborhood of Northeast Philadelphia, and the page gives no street address.

records.notes: The tier 1 file under this id held the Mitzvah Food Program, a separate food pantry program on the same Federation site. Its name, Bustleton pantry locations and hours, pantry phone and email, client form, food drive and drop-in first step were removed here because they describe a different program. The schedule days, times and season are sent as null on purpose to clear the pantry hours, and contacts.phone was changed to the cemetery contact. The Mitzvah Food Program is in leads_only. The cemetery page names a 2025 annual report but gives no month, so last_sign_of_life is left out. The FAQ states no volunteer criteria, work-day schedule, cost or dress guidance. Har Jehuda's location is not on the page, so it is not listed.

records.name: Friends of Laurel Hill and West Laurel Hill Cemeteries
records.summary: A nonprofit that helps look after two historic cemeteries, Laurel Hill in Philadelphia and West Laurel Hill in Bala Cynwyd. Volunteers help restore monuments and grounds, and the group runs tours and events.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers help with events, tour guiding, archive and records work, arboretum plantings and special projects. Volunteers must be 18 or older, and students can arrange internships.

schedule.text: Grounds open 7 am to 7 pm from spring through fall, and 7 am to 5 pm in winter. Volunteers pick the days and mornings or afternoons they can come, and the page lists no set shifts.

cost.text: Grounds admission is free every day. Friends memberships start at $25 a year for ages 21 to 40, or $50 a year for one person. Private tours are paid, and the tours page lists no public tour price.

first_step.how: Start the online volunteer application at laurelhillphl.com/support/volunteer, or email volunteers@laurelhillphl.com to join the list for events and planting days.
first_step.basis: Volunteering needs an online application with a membership step, and the page describes no beginner program. Visitors can walk the grounds free, so a first visit needs no application.
first_step.what_to_expect: The application asks which areas interest you, such as tour guiding, archives, events or planting, and which days and times you can come. For a first look, walk the grounds during gate hours or join one of the dated public tours on the tours page. The page does not mention an orientation, so ask what a new volunteer is trained to do.
first_visit_tips: Check gate hours first: 7 am to 7 pm from spring through fall, and 7 am to 5 pm in winter.
Laurel Hill East is in Philadelphia at 3822 Ridge Ave, and West Laurel Hill is in Bala Cynwyd, so confirm which cemetery a tour or event is at.
The free audio tour app covers Laurel Hill East and lets you plan a walk on your own.
Questions about tours go to tours@laurelhillphl.com or 215.228.8200.

records.notes: Tier 1 said probably_active with no dated evidence. The tours page lists two dated public tours (Oct 9 and Oct 10, 2026) and says the calendar may show more, so status is now active. Public tour prices are not listed; only private tour prices are. The volunteer application includes a Friends membership step, but no page says whether membership is required to volunteer, so ask. The visit page gives no accessibility, parking or transit details, so access is not set. The phone 610-668-9900 is the West Laurel Hill line; the East line is 215.228.8200. The events calendar was not read.

Nulls in the file were sent on purpose to clear values that do not belong to the group or have no dated source; the importer should confirm these clear.
